subject: Embed index reconciliation & priming — decision memo and next steps
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Emily Chen <emily.chen@atlassearch.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 28 Jul 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Embed index reconciliation & priming — decision memo and next steps

Emily — thanks for the deep-dive earlier. This thread is to lock the approach for the index reconciliation and priming we discussed (so we can handoff to CS and Implementation next week). High-level proposal below, followed by a short checklist and ask.

Goals
- Ensure search recall parity with existing TF-IDF index by seeding vectorstore with prioritized doc subsets.
- Keep downstream Rerank evaluation deterministic during cutover to validate model swap impact.

Proposed phased approach (4 waves)
1) Wave 0 — smoke: 1k high-frequency docs (daily top queries) for latency/compatibility tests.
2) Wave 1 — priority seeding: 50k docs (help center + product pages) to validate recall and rerank deltas.
3) Wave 2 — bulk backfill: remaining 450k documents in parallel batches with backpressure.
4) Wave 3 — priming & QA: priming sets, rerank A/B on canary traffic, final cutover.

Vector DB considerations
- Primary store: we recommend an existing managed vector DB (they support immediate shard reconfiguration) — AtlasSearch has good SKU fit; otherwise use Redwood-managed index for the first 2 waves.
- Document schema: include doc_id, source_type, created_at, raw_text, embed_version. We attached a sample mapping (index_mapping_sample.csv).

Rerank evaluation plan
- Fixed prompt set (100 queries) for each wave, baseline (current ranker), candidate reranker, and metric suite (MRR, P@1, recall@5).
- We'll run deterministic seeds and store per-query outputs to reproduce regressions. Spec attached (rerank_eval_spec.pdf).

Operational asks for AtlasSearch
- Confirm preferred vector DB (managed by you vs. Redwood-managed) by Fri 31 Jul.
- Provide a small dump (S3 link) of top-100k docs for Wave 1 by Mon 2 Aug.

Attachments: index_mapping_sample.csv (csv), rerank_eval_spec.pdf (pdf)

Thanks — I’ll synthesize into a formal handoff doc once we confirm the DB choice.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marcus@redwood.com
From: Emily Chen <emily.chen@atlassearch.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Cc: Aisha Tan <aisha.t@atlassearch.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 29 Jul 2026 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Embed index reconciliation & priming — decision memo and next steps

Marcus — this looks good and aligns with our internal ops. A couple quick clarifications: 

1) Vector DB: we prefer to try Redwood-managed index for Wave 0/1 to minimize infra work, then evaluate moving to our managed cluster in Wave 2. Is that supported?
2) Dump timing: we can provide an S3 path for the top-100k by Aug 2, but can you confirm an expected ingest SLA (seconds per 1k docs) for Wave 1 so our infra can provision?

Also: small ask on rerank evals — can you include an audio-transcript bucket in Wave 1? ~8k transcripts that need slightly different tokenization.

Thanks,
Emily
Emily Chen
Head of Search Product, AtlasSearch
emily.chen@atlassearch.com
From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Emily Chen <emily.chen@atlassearch.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 30 Jul 2026 11:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Embed index reconciliation & priming — decision memo and next steps

Emily — yes on both counts. Quick responses: 

- Redwood-managed index for Wave 0/1 is fine; we’ll run Wave 0 smoke on a small dedicated pool (no infra changes required on your side). For Wave 2 the plan is to migrate the index or sync to your managed cluster; we’ll provide an exporter tool and run a reconciliation pass.
- Ingest SLA: based on our tests, baseline is ~8–12 seconds per 1k docs when embeddings are computed inline and the documents average 750 tokens. With precomputed embeddings the ingest speed jumps to ~1–2 seconds per 1k. I recommend precomputing if your pipeline can.
- Audio transcripts: noted. We’ll add a tokenization step in the mapping (field: audio_transcript_text) and run a small rerank sanity subset for transcripts inside Wave 1.

Next steps (expected owners & dates)
- AtlasSearch: confirm DB preference (Redwood-managed first) — owner: Emily — due: 2026-07-31.
- AtlasSearch: upload Wave1 S3 dump (top-100k) — owner: Aisha — due: 2026-08-02.
- Redwood: prepare index mapping and ingestion playbook + exporter script — owner: Marcus — due: 2026-08-01 (attached: index_mapping_sample.csv).
- Redwood: prepare rerank eval config and notebook — owner: Naomi — due: 2026-08-04 (attached spec).

I’ll follow up with a short runbook and the handoff ticket to CS once we have the DB confirmation.

—Marcus
From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 01 Aug 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: AtlasSearch embed cutover — final decision and handoff checklist

Team — quick internal summary (do not share externally until Emily confirms the DB choice):

Final decisions confirmed with AtlasSearch (pending Emily’s stamp):
- Use Redwood-managed index for Wave 0 and Wave 1. AtlasSearch will host from Wave 2 onward.
- Wave 1 will include the audio transcript subset (8k) under the field audio_transcript_text.

Immediate internal action items:
- Naomi: create the rerank_eval notebook with fixed-seed sampling and include MR R, P@1, recall@5 metrics. Deadline: 2026-08-04. Attach rerank_eval_spec.pdf to the ticket.
- Jordan: finalize the ingestion playbook; include guidance for precomputed embeddings and include backpressure knobs (batch size, concurrency, retry). Deadline: 2026-08-01. Attach index_mapping_sample.csv.
- Ben: open the CS handoff ticket and schedule a 45-min playbook walkthru with AtlasSearch for Wed 2026-08-04. Put tentative invite on Emily’s calendar once we get the S3 link.

Notes on risk & mitigations:
- Risk: rerank regressions when moving from small seeded index to full backfill. Mitigation: hold out a fixed validation set and run nightly regression checks during Wave 2.
- Risk: ingestion rate variability. Mitigation: recommend precomputed embeddings where possible and set a conservative concurrency ceiling.

Attachments referenced for tickets: index_mapping_sample.csv, rerank_eval_spec.pdf

Thanks — I’ll push the final handoff doc into the CS folder when Emily confirms.

—Marcus
